prerequisites: Basic knowledge of geometry and representation systems
Graphic Expression course from the first semester of the first year

learning_outcomes.text: That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Knowledge and capacities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Advanced spatial vision capacity and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, as well as by computer-aided design applications.
Ability to work, lead, and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: II. Industrial Drawing and its Applications.

Topic 1: General representation standards in industrial drawing. Introduction to Industrial Drawing. Standardization: formats, scales and lines. Other standardized views. Cuts, sections and breaks. Performing development exercises.

Topic 2: Representation standards in the manufacturing of industrial products. Standardized dimensioning. Surface states. Dimensional tolerances. Geometrical tolerances. Performing development exercises. Use of multilingual documentation.

Topic 3: Conventional representation of standardized elements. Removable fasteners: threads, screws, nuts and studs. Keys and keyways. Washers and pins. Fixed fasteners: welding. Rivets. Other standardized elements: shafts and axles. Centering holes. Springs. Bars and profiles. Performing development exercises using Reverse Engineering to obtain results from real products using 3D Scanner techniques and obtaining real models using Rapid Prototyping techniques with 3D Printing.

Topic 4: Representation of industrial products. Assemblies. Disassembly drawings. List of elements. Performing product design exercises or complex assemblies and the study of their design, safety, economy and manufacturing requirements. Use of multilingual documentation.
Topic 5: Representation of industrial installations and processes. Performing development exercises.
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical-practical exam on theoretical and operational knowledge
Completion of practices and assignments (individual or group, including CAD practice and 3D CAD software handling tests)

assessment_rules: The course is passed if a weighted grade between theory and practice of 5 points is obtained (with a minimum of 4 points in both parts), being considered approved or failed in its entirety in each call. The personal work grade will be maintained during the academic year's calls.
